The pes-cavus target is an acquired-claw-foot musculoskeletal identity; the evidence base is inherited-neuropathy cohort epidemiology, so the CMT-population anchor is recorded as a phenotype-population guard on the edge.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 27 (2026-09-23): one bounded pes-cavus association authored from inherited-neuropathy cohort evidence (Inherited Neuropathies Consortium 71% foot-deformity prevalence; CMT4C early-onset series); the neuro-proprioceptive mechanism is hypothesis-class, and the CMT-population anchor is guarded because the primary identity is broader than CMT.

Generic peripheral-neuropathy and the named mononeuropathy identities have no edges and were not treated as blocking; this edge is authored per-identity from early-onset-specific literature under the amputation-family precedent that each identity waits for its own level-appropriate evidence.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: In the Inherited Neuropathies Consortium cohort, foot deformities were reported in 71% of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease patients and 30% underwent orthopedic surgery (Laura 2018), and the CMT4C case series documents pes cavus appearing among the earliest manifestations of early-onset hereditary neuropathy (Okhovat 2026); early-onset hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy is the classic clinical association of the pes-cavus phenotype.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the 71% prevalence is CMT-population cohort data and the identity spans acquired and hereditary early-onset etiologies, pes cavus can be congenital or independently acquired (trauma, compartment syndrome, spasticity), and an individual's deformity may precede, accompany, or be unrelated to the neuropathy; chronologic primacy cannot be established from population data.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized denervation-imbalance foot-deformity pathway: early-onset motor-sensory neuropathy produces chronic weakness of intrinsic foot muscles with relative sparing of extrinsic flexors and peroneus brevis-type imbalance, so the denervated foot develops progressive plantar-flexed first ray, hindfoot varus, and high medial longitudinal arch under continued weight bearing; the same imbalance also recruits peroneus longus overaction in some phenotypes. The individual pathway from a documented neuropathy to a documented deformity must be established case by case from electrodiagnostics, genetics, and orthopedic evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The population anchor is CMT-specific cohort data applied to a broader early-onset identity; congenital and independently acquired pes cavus must be excluded, the deformity's onset chronology relative to the neuropathy requires documentation, and the denervation-imbalance mechanism is hypothesis-class anatomy rather than quantified individual causation; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented early-onset peripheral neuropathy with electrodiagnostic or genetic confirmation; documented pes-cavus morphology by validated foot examination or imaging with onset chronology; exclusion of congenital deformity, prior trauma, or spasticity as the deformity driver; CMT genetic testing or equivalent etiologic workup where indicated; orthopedic and neurology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Congenital pes cavus or developmental deformity unrelated to neuropathy
Prior foot trauma, compartment syndrome, or crush injury
Spastic hemiplegia or cerebral palsy-driven deformity
Idiopathic pes cavus with incidental electrodiagnostic abnormality
Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease as an independent inherited diagnosis rather than the documented early-onset identity

evidenceGaps: Documented early-onset peripheral neuropathy with electrodiagnostic or genetic confirmation; documented pes-cavus morphology by validated foot examination or imaging with onset chronology; exclusion of congenital deformity, prior trauma, or spasticity as the deformity driver; CMT genetic testing or equivalent etiologic workup where indicated; orthopedic and neurology assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the hereditary-neuropathy-to-pes-cavus association is clinically classic and cohort-quantified, but the primary identity is broader than the CMT evidence base, the mechanism is hypothesis-class, and congenital or traumatic alternatives are common; no causation is forced.
